senses.gloss: m. (כשט = קָשַׁט) ornament, decoration; toilet article.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 9:9:2">Y. Ned. IX, end, 41ᶜ</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00153"><he>עָדַן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 63b:11">Sabb. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ … טמא</he> any piece of jewelry, however small, is susceptible of uncleanness.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 8:33">Tosef. Sabb. VIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 9:33">IX</cite>), 33 <he>אם לת׳</he> if the eye paint is used for cosmetic purposes; (<cite ref="Shabbat 80a:7">Sabb. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>לקשט</he>); a. fr.—Pl. <he>תַּכְשִׁיטִים</he>, <he>תַּכְשִׁיטִין</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 60b:15-16">B. Bath. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>עושה … תַּכְשִׁיטֶיהָ וכ׳</he> a woman may do all her cosmetic painting, but should leave some part undone (in memory of the destruction of the Temple).

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 6:4">Sabb. VI, 4</cite> <he>ת׳ הן לו</he> they (the arms) are man’s ornaments (therefore one may wear them when going out on the Sabbath), opp. <cite ref="C01076"><he>גְּנַאי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 6:3:3">Y. Keth. VI, 30ᵈ</cite> top <he>תַּקְשִׁיטִין לעשותן וכ׳</he> if the wife brought him jewelry to be turned into coin, the Denar is charged to him for a Denar and a half; <he>דינר לעשותן תק׳ וכ׳</he> if she brought him coined gold to be made into jewelry, the Denars are taken for their value; a. fr.
